inputs.text: Look, we are once again seeing the predictable fallout of a system that prioritizes property owners over the fundamental human right to shelter. Taoiseach Micheál Martin has the nerve to boast in Limerick this past week that housing tenancies have increased, completely glossing over the human cost of his own administration's policies. While the Government pats itself on the back for introducing new rules on March 1 forcing landlords to provide six-year leases for tenants, working-class families and vulnerable people are bearing the brunt of the backlash. The reality on the ground—which the establishment tries to sweep under the rug—is a shameful rise in eviction notices and homelessness, with the numbers of people in emergency accommodation nationally increasing again. This is what happens when systemic reform is half-hearted and leaves loopholes for landlords to weaponize against tenants. Instead of confronting the structural inequality driving this housing crisis, the political elite just spin the numbers to protect the status quo while the most vulnerable are pushed out onto the streets.
